messages:
emily (PM): quick sync — i'm drafting the PRD for graceful degradation behavior for hosted + dedicated + private. need clear acceptance criteria for latency sLOs, error-budget actions, and rollout gating. any immediate red flags?

darren (eng-reliability): +1. we should be explicit about p50/p95/p99 and a tail SLO (eg p99.9). propose we define by payload class (<512, 512-2048). also need error-budget burn thresholds that map to actions (notify, degrade, throttle, rollback).

liam (infra): for hosted: p50 120ms / p95 300ms / p99 800ms for small requests (<512). medium requests: p50 250ms / p95 600ms / p99 1.6s. Dedicated customers can opt for looser p95 (400ms) but stronger isolation. on error-budgets: suggest warn @ 25%, start routing by policy at 50% (split traffic to cheaper variant), full degrade at 80%.

emily (PM): ok. acceptance criteria draft: 1) SLO table by request class + model family; 2) automated actions: at 50% 1h -> canary to smaller model variant; at 80% 5m -> return 503 + structured degrade payload; 3) regression tests for quality; 4) rollout gating in console + per-customer opt-in for Dedicated. thoughts?

sophia (eng-ml): switching model variants is risky — must run automated evals against our prompt suite. acceptance criterion: no >5% relative increase in hallucination/regression on critical prompts when degraded. also require an on-call quick-check dashboard showing quality metrics for any degradation window.

maya (customer-success): customers want predictable UX. if we degrade, return a machine-readable note so apps can decide: ``{"status":"degraded", "model":"r1-small", "reason":"latency"}``. also include human-readable banner for downstream clients.

darren (eng-reliability): operational tests: 1) synthetic load / KV-cache pressure test; 2) chaos test (region failover + model variant fallback); 3) long-tail test for p99.9 with token windows. acceptance: all tests pass in staging with no silent data loss. add playbook steps for manual rollback.

liam (infra): infra notes: feature flags for degradation must be local-enabled for private/on-prem (no outbound FF calls). console needs a per-customer error budget ledger and ability to pin fallback model list. also add metric + alert thresholds: e.g., burn rate > 3 for 10m -> pager.

emily (PM): edge cases to call out in PRD: - private deployments: ensure on-device fallbacks + local config - streaming responses: handle partial token emission when falling back - batched requests: ensure deterministic degradation (don't mix variants in same batch) - quota-exhaustion vs degrade (distinct paths).

oncall-bot: deploy-preview created: pr/4527 — contains initial graceful-degrade RFC draft (link: https://redwood/gh/pr/4527) :eyes:

emily (PM): i'll update the PRD & RFC with these bullets. next steps: @darren to draft SLO table + error-budget-actions, @sophia to provide eval prompts and acceptance thresholds, @liam to list infra gating requirements (flags, ledger, alerts). sync friday 10am PT? :calendar:

maya (customer-success): i'll collect top 10 customer asks to include in the rollout FAQ.

darren (eng-reliability): i'll post SLO table by EOD wed.

emily (PM): perfect — thanks all :thumbsup:
